newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish police urge vigilance after firebomb.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish police urge vigilance after firebomb.

text.p: A suspected guerrilla fire bomb destroyed a clothing shop in Belfast on Wednesday and police urged the business community to be vigilant.
Northern Ireland police said the shop, off a main city centre street, had been gutted and they suspected some type of incendiary device had detonated.
Security sources said no-one had admitted the attack but they were trying to establish whether it was a type previously used by Irish Republican Army guerrillas.
The IRA, which is fighting to end British rule, has stepped up hostilities in the past month with a series of rocket and bomb attacks and a shooting, in which a policeman was wounded.
Pro-British Loyalist hardliners are suspected of launching retaliatory attacks on two Catholic civilians who are well-known republicans opposed to British sovereignty.

Before declaring a September 1994 truce, which collapsed last February, the IRA waged a bombing war against so-called "economic targets" in town centres, using explosives and small firebombs to lethal effect.
